title: Airbus A320 family
wiki_lead:
The Airbus A320 family is a series of narrow-body airliners developed and produced by Airbus, and is the best-selling airliner ever built. The A320 aircraft programme was launched in March 1984, first flew on 22 February 1987, and was introduced in April 1988 by Air France.
The first member of the family was followed by the stretched A321 (first delivered in January 1994), the shorter A319 (April 1996), and the shortest variant, the A318 (July 2003).
Final assembly takes place in Toulouse in France; Hamburg in Germany; Tianjin in China since 2009; and Mobile, Alabama, in the United States since April 2016.
The twinjet has a six-abreast economy cross-section and came with either CFM56-5A or -5B, or IAE V2500 turbofan engines, except the A318. The A318 has either two CFM56-5B engines or a pair of PW6000 engines in place of the IAE V2500.
The family pioneered the use of digital fly-by-wire and side-stick flight controls in airliners.
Variants offer maximum take-off weights from 68 to 93.5 tonnes (150,000 to 206,000 lb), with a range of 5,740–6,940 kilometres (3,570–4,320 mi; 3,100–3,750 nmi).
The 31.4 m (103 ft) long A318 typically accommodates 107 to 132 passengers.
The 124-156 seat A319 is 33.8 m (111 ft) long.
The A320 is 37.6 m (123 ft) long and can accommodate 150 to 186 passengers.
The 44.5 m (146 ft) A321 offers 185 to 230 seats.
The Airbus Corporate Jets are modified business jet versions of the standard commercial variants.
In December 2010, Airbus announced the re-engined A320neo (new engine option), which entered service with Lufthansa in January 2016. With more efficient turbofans and improvements including "sharklet" winglets, it offers up to 15% better fuel economy. The previous A320 generation was renamed A320ceo (current engine option).
American Airlines is the largest A320 family operator with 498 aircraft in its fleet, while IndiGo is the largest customer with 930 aircraft on order as of October 2026. A total of 20,598 A320 family aircraft have been ordered of which 12,955 units have been delivered and 11,422 units are in service with more than 375 operators. It overtook the Boeing 737 family in terms of total fleet size in 2017, in terms of total orders in October 2019 and in terms of total deliveries in September 2025. The global A320 fleet had completed more than 176 million flights over 328 million block hours since its entry into service. The A320ceo initially competed with the 737 Classic and the MD-80, then their successors, the 737 Next Generation (737NG) and the MD-90 respectively, while the 737 MAX is Boeing's response to the A320neo.

grok_lead: The Airbus A320 family is a family of narrow-body, twin-engine jet airliners developed and produced by Airbus, consisting of the A318, A319, A320, and A321 variants in their original current engine option (ceo) configuration, as well as the more efficient new engine option (neo) versions including the A319neo, A320neo, A321neo, A321LR, and A321XLR, designed primarily for short- to medium-haul flights with capacities ranging from 120 to 244 passengers. Launched in March 1984 with initial orders from Air Inter and British Caledonian, the A320 pioneered fly-by-wire flight controls in commercial aviation, entering service in 1988 and setting new standards for efficiency, safety, and passenger comfort in the single-aisle market. Subsequent variants expanded the lineup: the A321 in 1994 for higher capacity, the A319 in 1996 for shorter routes, and the A318 in 2003 as a smaller regional option, while the neo family, announced in 2007 and entering service with the A320neo in 2016, incorporates advanced engines from Pratt & Whitney or CFM International, sharklet wingtip devices, and aerodynamic improvements for up to 20% lower fuel consumption and COâ emissions, a 50% reduction in noise footprint, and 14% lower cash operating costs per seat compared to ceo models. Key features across the family include a wide single-aisle cabin (3.7 meters in diameter, allowing 18-inch-wide economy seats), a common type rating for pilot training, and the Airspace by Airbus interior with larger overhead bins (60% more bag capacity), customizable LED lighting, larger windows, and enhanced connectivity for superior passenger experience. Performance varies by variant, with ranges from 3,450 nautical miles for the A320neo to 4,700 nautical miles for the A321XLR, enabling transcontinental operations, and the family supports up to 50% sustainable aviation fuel (SAF) blends today, targeting 100% by 2030. As of the end of October 2026, the A320 family holds the position of the world's best-selling and most-delivered aircraft program, with 20,598 gross orders from more than 300 operators, 12,955 deliveries, and a backlog of 7,643 aircraft, having accumulated over 380 million flight hours and demonstrating high operational reliability. In October 2025, the program became the most delivered commercial airliner type in history, surpassing the Boeing 737. Its versatility serves low-cost carriers like IndiGo and Ryanair as well as full-service airlines for routes from regional hops to long-haul missions, underscoring its role in shaping modern commercial aviation amid demands for efficiency and sustainability.
